autodesk_sponsored_deployment.date_basis: Selected alternate-history agreement day after the historical 30 January founding meeting; formally adopted by Autodesk after its 26 April incorporation.
autodesk_sponsored_deployment.objective: Deliver AutoCAD 1.0 for Artemis/AIONix for the joint November 1982 COMDEX presentation; November release-quality build is the commitment, with commercial shipment subject to acceptance rather than automatically deferred to December.
autodesk_sponsored_deployment.sponsor: Adam through Logix; AION Software and AION Labs provide development and hardware support.
autodesk_sponsored_deployment.commercial_terms: Non-exclusive funded development. Autodesk retains its software ownership and cross-platform business; clear the underlying Interact contribution/porting rights with the founders, including Mike Riddle. Logix supplies distribution and joint marketing, without a source buyout or forced platform exclusivity.

team_environment.workstations: Supply an Artemis PRO with 1 MiB RAM, local storage and available display to each assigned developer, plus shared build/test and spare machines as the agreed staffing plan requires. No invented fixed team size.
team_environment.software: Install the entire AION Development System — Team Edition: C Development Environment 2, ERA compiler/linker/debugger and validated floating-point math library; source repository, branches/reviews, tasks, collaboration, reproducible builds, release labels and target testing.
team_environment.network: Supply network adapters, hub, cabling, configured accounts and project permissions, and dedicated Artemis PRO server capacity. Scale sponsored server/license deployments to the whole team within qualified concurrency; the retail four-session entitlement is not silently unlimited.
team_environment.storage: The standard 5 MB disk is inadequate as a presumed whole-team repository/build archive. Fund and qualify larger storage, additional volumes/servers, independent backup media, restore tests and off-machine source archives; capacities follow measured source/build/history budgets.
team_environment.support: Fund dedicated Autodesk engineering time, AION compiler/runtime and integration specialists, installation, training, documentation, replacement hardware, plotter access and on-site support through release. Retail onboarding/support-hour caps do not limit this separately sponsored agreement.
team_environment.early_graphics: January work uses available Artemis PRO displays and a stable software implementation of the graphics API. Supply 64 KiB/Color Pro engineering samples and mouse prototypes when qualified; do not make January work depend on the June professional hardware.
team_environment.professional_handover: Around June 1982 deliver the 128 KiB professional card and Logix Mono Pro 17 to the development and QA team, alongside the 64 KiB colour card/Color Pro 14 and mouse. This supersedes the earlier proposed January 17-inch prototype handover.

Final staffing/procurement approval remains open; the provision is not a funding cap.
autodesk_sponsored_deployment.historical_distinction: Historical COMDEX introduction was 29 November; historical AutoCAD 1.0 shipment was December 1982. The funded Artemis release target is an explicit alternate-history acceleration.
autodesk_sponsored_deployment.professional_hardware_revision: COMDEX November revision adds explicit inherited modes, palette sequencing and five-sprite compatibility; preserve June development handover. See dated revisions in the catalog.
